The transition from linear "take-make-dispose" industrial models to a circular economy has
emerged as a cornerstone of contemporary environmental policy. Unlike conventional recycling,
which often downgrades material quality through energy-intensive reprocessing, circular design
prioritises durability, modularity, and closed-loop resource recovery from the very inception of a
product. When electronics, textiles, and construction materials are engineered for disassembly and
remanufacturing, virgin resource extraction diminishes substantially, alleviating pressure on fragile
ecosystems. Nevertheless, scaling circularity confronts formidable structural barriers, including
fragmented reverse-logistics networks, higher upfront manufacturing costs, and entrenched
consumer preferences for disposable convenience. Bridging this gap requires fiscal instruments—
such as extended producer responsibility mandates and differential taxation—that internalise
ecological externalities into market prices.

Comprehension Passage – II (Questions 46 – 50): Read the following passage carefully and
answer the questions that follow.
Long before the advent of modern satellite navigation, Polynesian wayfinders traversed thousands
of miles of open Pacific Ocean without compasses, sextants, or written charts. Their extraordinary
navigational system relied on an intimate, multisensory reading of the marine environment.
Wayfinders memorised the rising and setting azimuths of over two hundred stars, using a mental
"star compass" to maintain bearings across trackless waters. During overcast nights or daylight
hours, they steered by interpreting the subtle interference patterns of ocean swells refracting
around distant, unseen islands, alongside the flight trajectories of land-nesting seabirds such as
terns and noddies. Far from being intuitive guesswork, traditional Polynesian navigation was an
empirical science transmitted across generations through rigorous oral pedagogy and practical
apprenticeship.

By anchoring their canoes until clear skies returned

ଅସମ୍ଭବ । ଯେଉଁ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ସମୟର ସଦୁପଯୋଗ କରି ନିଜର କର୍ତ୍ତବ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପାଦନ କରନ୍ତି, ସେମାନେ ଜୀବନରେ ସଫଳତାର ଶୀର୍ଷରେ
ପହଞ୍ଚିପାରନ୍ତି । ଅପରପକ୍ଷେ, ଆଳସ୍ୟ ଓ ଦୀର୍ଘସୂତ୍ରତା ମନୁଷ୍ୟକୁ ପତନ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଟାଣିନିଏ । ପ୍ରକୃତିର ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଉପାଦାନ—ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟ, ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର,
ଋତୁଚକ୍ର—ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ସମୟାନୁବର୍ତ୍ତିତାର ନିୟମରେ ପରିଚାଳିତ ହୁଅନ୍ତି । ତେଣୁ ଛାତ୍ରଜୀବନରୁ ହିଁ ସମୟାନୁବର୍ତ୍ତିତା ଓ ଶୃଙ୍ଖଳାର
ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ଗଢ଼ିତୋଳିବା ଉଚିତ ।
